title: Extending Beacon to Hindi: Cultural Adaptation Drives Cross-Lingual Sycophancy

bias_targets.methodology: Using a single-turn forced-choice benchmark (adapted from Beacon) to measure how often models prioritize agreeing with a user's stated preference over providing factually grounded or principled responses across factual, opinion, and advice scenarios.
Comparing sycophancy rates on culturally adapted Hindi prompts against literal Hindi translations to isolate the impact of culturally grounded framing and social deference norms.
Evaluating sycophancy rate differences between English original prompts and matched literal Hindi translations to measure language encoding effects independent of cultural adaptation.
